title: when VAN LIFE is risky!! | shipping our home to COLOMBIA
description:
We LOVED our trip with San Blas Adventures through the San Blas Islands. If you want to book a trip with them, get 5% off your trip with San Blas Adventures by using the code "SanBlasT". (This code does not expire, so use it anytime!) https://sanblasadventures.com/

Our Course: https://thematneys.co/course

INSTRUCTIONS FOR SHIPPING A VEHICLE:
If you haven't already, watch our video about dropping our van off to be shipped in Panama: https://youtu.be/wwog007ASrU

We picked up our van in Colombia without an agent, something that isn't very common, but if you or someone in your party speaks Spanish, is VERY doable. But if you feel more comfortable hiring an agent, your agent from Panama can give you a recommendation. We decided not to hire an agent in order to save the agent fees, allegedly around $200-$300.

Step 1: Find out when your van is ready to be picked up. Instructions: Email your agent in Panama to find out if your van is loaded off the ship and is ready to be picked up. If you are still waiting, you can still do Steps 2-4.

Step 2: Acquire the NAVES fees invoices. Instructions: Contact NAVES (your agent in Panama can give you the correct contact info). They had to process our invoices (they’ll need pictures of some documents like your passport and title), and it took more than 24 hours. This is something you should get started as soon as possible, even before your van is cleared.

Step 3: Acquire your Bill of Lading. Instructions: We printed out the 4 invoices NAVES sent us and they required us to pay them at ITAÚ bank. We found one very close to the NAVES office in Manga (a neighborhood in Cartagena). On Google Maps, it comes up as Helm Bank but is in fact ITAÚ. Once we had paid our invoices, we went to the NAVES office with proof of payment and they processed our Bill of Lading.

Step 4: Get your TIP (permit to drive in the country). Instructions: Go to the DIAN office (also located in Manga) to get your TIP moving. They might tell you to go to the port and get pictures of your vehicle there and a picture of the vin number on the vehicle. They’ll need certain documents like copies of your passport, your Bill of Lading, copies of your title, etc. We didn’t have everything when we first went (the pictures in particular), but they began the process anyways. (FYI, you’ll need your TIP to pick up your vehicle.)

Step 5: Pay your port fees. Instructions: We made a mistake and did not pay the extra port fees before going to the port. I would contact your agent in Panama and also contact the port to find out what port fees you need to pay. Acquire those invoices. We had to pay them at Banco de Bogotá. Make sure you have proof of payment.

Step 6: Get your vehicle! Instructions: Go to the port (ours was Port Bahía) with your TIP, proof of payment of your port fees, and Bill of Lading. You’ll also need all of your documents you usually need at borders like your passport and title, etc. You also might call ahead to see if you can schedule an appointment. We had to wait for 2 hours for the appointment they scheduled us when we got there. If you don’t call, just make sure you get there early enough in the day in case they need to schedule an appointment for you as well. Once you’re there, they’ll tell you the documents you need and where exactly to go, so just follow their instructions. Only one person will be able to go to acquire the van, so be prepared for that.

Step 7: Drive your van out and get exploring!

ABOUT THE EPISODE:
After hearing horror story after horror story of other travelers who had had their belongings stolen from their van life homes after shipping them, we were terrified that we had taken too great of a risk. What if we picked up our van at port and found it to be empty with all of our possessions stolen? Van life in Colombia and the rest of South America is so exciting to us, but are we willing to risk it all?

About The Matneys:
We're Christian and Aubry, a couple traveling North and South America in our converted Sprinter Van. On The Matneys, we love chatting about the reality of living in a van, what van life allows us to do, and how traveling to new places with new cultures can really open your eyes to so much about the world, our own country, and ourselves. Our little home is simple, but it takes us to the most magical paradises in the world.
